description_full: BlackLine, Inc. provides cloud-based solutions to automate and streamline accounting and finance operations in the United States and internationally. It offers financial close and consolidation solutions, such as account reconciliations that provides a centralized workspace for users to collaborate on account reconciliations; transaction matching, which analyzes and reconciles individual transactions; task management to create and manage processes and task lists; and financial reporting analytics that enables analysis and validation of financial data. The company also provides journal entry, which allows users to generate, review, and post manual journal entries; variance analysis that offers anomalous fluctuations in balance sheet and income statement account balances; compliance, an integrated solution that facilitates compliance-related initiatives, consolidates project management, and provides visibility over control self-assessments and testing; and smart close for SAP solution. In addition, it offers credit and risk, collection, dispute and deduction, and team and task management, as well as AR intelligence, electronic invoicing and payment, and cash application solutions. Further, the company provides intercompany create functionality that stores permissions and business logic exceptions by entity, service, and transaction type; intercompany balance and resolve, which records an organization's intercompany transactions; and netting and settlement that enables open intercompany transactions, which integrate with treasury systems. Additionally, it offers implementation, optimization, live and web-based training, and support services. The company sells its solutions primarily through direct sales force to multinational corporations, large domestic enterprises, and mid-market companies across various industries. The company was incorporated in 2001 and is headquartered in Woodland Hills, California.

financial_summary: BlackLine, Inc. is a small-cap technology business with a $1.7B market cap on $700M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +10% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size. Operating margins are expanding by +3.5pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at -16% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 76% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $161M in free cash flow — roughly 23 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 6.92× so those profits are backed by real cash.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin 2.5× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 14.0% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and stock-based comp at 13% of revenue is silent dilution an owner has to account for, and insiders hold 9.6% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.2× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
